Save and restore model state with Orbax

Source: R/callbacks.R
callback_orbax_checkpoint.Rd

Saves model weights and optimizer state asynchronously with Orbax. On the JAX backend, checkpointing is coordinated across hosts. The Python orbax-checkpoint package is required.

Usage

callback_orbax_checkpoint(
  directory,
  monitor = "val_loss",
  verbose = 0L,
  save_best_only = FALSE,
  mode = "auto",
  save_freq = "epoch",
  initial_value_threshold = NULL,
  max_to_keep = 1L,
  save_on_background = TRUE,
  save_weights_only = FALSE
)

Arguments

directory

Directory in which to save checkpoints.

monitor

Metric name to monitor.

verbose

Verbosity mode, 0 or 1.

save_best_only

Whether to save only when monitor improves.

mode

One of "auto", "min", or "max".

save_freq

"epoch" or an integer number of batches between saves.

initial_value_threshold

Initial best value for monitor.

max_to_keep

Maximum number of recent checkpoints to retain. Use NULL to retain all checkpoints.

save_on_background

Whether to save asynchronously in the background.

save_weights_only

Whether to save only trainable and non-trainable variables, excluding model configuration, optimizer state, and assets.

Value

A Callback instance that can be passed to fit.keras.src.models.model.Model().

Examples

checkpoint <- callback_orbax_checkpoint(
  directory = tempfile("orbax-checkpoints-"),
  monitor = "val_accuracy",
  mode = "max",
  save_best_only = TRUE
)
model |> fit(x, y, validation_split = 0.2, callbacks = list(checkpoint))
